summary: Regression check after code-quality refactor (receipt XSS escaping, AuthContext/OfflineContext useMemo, Dashboard useCallback). Backend: 99/99 pytest passed (backend_test.py + test_new_features.py) against the public preview URL. Frontend: verified admin+kasir auth & role gating, session persistence, POS checkout end-to-end (order types, category filter, cart, discount, cash/QRIS payment, change), receipt print + Cetak Ulang reprint, Dashboard reload on date change + Gemini AI summary, offline sale queue/auto-sync, and admin CRUD (category, product w/ cost, edit, sold-out toggle, table, purchase, stock opname, cash in/out). XSS escaping explicitly proven with a seeded product named 'TEST_XSS & "q"' - receipt markup contained <img ... >, &, " and fired no JS dialog. Zero console/page errors in all flows. No regressions found from the refactor; 2 pre-existing defects and 1 backend data-integrity bug reported below.

critical.issue: Order number is generated with count_documents on today's prefix, which is not atomic. Concurrent order creation produces duplicate order numbers - DB currently holds GAK-20260820-0004 three times (found via aggregation). Duplicate receipt numbers break reprint/audit traceability. Fix: atomic $inc counter document (findOneAndUpdate) per day + unique index on order_number.

minor.issue: No brute-force protection / lockout: unlimited failed attempts allowed for the same email (playbook expects lockout after ~5 failures). bcrypt hashes are correct ($2b$12$) and seed_admin is idempotent (updates hash when ADMIN_PASSWORD changes).
Cashier seed credentials are hardcoded in source ('kasir@grandaceh.com'/'kasir123'); should come from env vars like the admin seed.
allow_origins falls back to '*' when CORS_ORIGINS is unset. allow_credentials=False (JWT Bearer, no cookies) so it is not exploitable, but an explicit origin list is preferable.
Soft-delete only (active=false). Acceptable for history integrity, but test/seed rows accumulate invisibly in the DB - noted for future cleanup expectations.

ui_bugs.issue: Choosing a dine-in table for a table WITHOUT an open bill silently wipes the cart (setCart([])). Reproduced: added item then picked/switched table -> cart went from 1 item to 0 with no warning; the 'Ganti jenis transaksi' style confirm is not applied here. Cashier loses keyed-in items.

The sync-history + reconciliation view (data-testid=sync-history) is only reachable through open-queue-btn, which renders only while pendingCount > 0. After a successful sync the queue empties and the offline->official order-number reconciliation history becomes unreachable from the UI. Needs a persistent entry point.
cacheAt is read from localStorage during render without state/subscription, so 'Data ter-cache' only refreshes on re-render of the sidebar (stale timestamp possible).

action_items: HIGH: make order-number generation atomic (counter doc + unique index on orders.order_number); existing duplicate GAK-20260820-0004 (x3) should be reconciled.
MEDIUM: POS dine-in table selection must not silently discard an existing cart (merge, or confirm like switchType).
MEDIUM: expose sync history/reconciliation even when the offline queue is empty.
LOW: add login attempt throttling/lockout; move seeded kasir credentials to env; set explicit CORS_ORIGINS.
critical_code_review_comments: receipt.js esc() correctly covers all user-controlled interpolations (item name, order_number, cashier_name, order type label, payment method name, formatted date); numeric values go through rupiah() so they are safe. Verified end-to-end with a malicious product name.

AuthContext/OfflineContext useMemo+useCallback are dependency-correct; offline fallback to cached gak_user on network error still works (verified: reload while online keeps session, offline sale still authorised and queued).
Dashboard load useCallback([date]) + useEffect([load]) is correct - changing the date refetches the summary and resets the AI text.
gen_order_number using count_documents is the only real correctness bug found; it also means order numbers can regress if an order is hard-deleted.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of regression flows passed (3 pre-existing UX/reactivity defects reported)

rca_of_the_issue: Duplicate order numbers: gen_order_number() counts today's orders and appends count+1, so two concurrent POSTs (e.g. parallel pytest workers or two cashiers) read the same count and mint the same number; no unique index exists to reject it. POS cart wipe: selectTable() unconditionally executes setCart([]) in the else-branch when the picked table has no open_order_id, discarding items added before the table was chosen.
